# Summary

Interdisciplinary population health scientist and demographer working at the intersection of epidemiology and data science, with more than a decade of research on how incomplete and imperfect health information becomes population evidence. My work spans measurement bias and survey validation; mortality measurement, tool validation, and health information systems; and demographic inference under incomplete and misclassified data. I combine applied research with Bayesian, computational, and AI methods and build reusable software and data infrastructure with WHO and international partners. Author or coauthor of 23 peer-reviewed publications, including first-author and joint-first-author work in *Lancet Global Health*.

# Expertise

**Methods:** Bayesian and demographic estimation; mortality and cause-of-death modeling; survey methods, measurement error, validation, and monitoring; machine learning, pretrained language models, LLMs, and multimodal learning; evidence synthesis

**Computing:** R, Python, Julia, SQL, Stata; Hugging Face, Optuna; Azure, Snowflake, AWS

**Domains:** mortality surveillance and verbal autopsy; civil registration and vital statistics; health information systems; maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health; global health estimation; population health

# Experience

```{=latex}
\role{Postdoctoral Fellow}{May 2025 -- present}
\org{Institute for Population Research (from Feb 2026) and Health and Environment Modeling Laboratory, The Ohio State University}
```

- Core team member of CODA, a Gates Foundation-initiated international consortium developing AI-enabled cause-of-death determination: test multimodal fusion performance, contribute to model choice, development, and interpretation, and coauthor consortium papers.
- Research on language models, multimodal learning, and information sufficiency in verbal autopsy; first and corresponding author of a national multimodal cause-of-death benchmark released on *medRxiv*, and coauthor of a separate child-mortality benchmark presented as a NeurIPS 2026 poster by its first author.
- Teaching Assistant, SOCIOL 8607 Causal Modeling (Spring 2026): facilitated discussion and provided coding support.

```{=latex}
\role{Platform Manager and Core Developer, Reference Data Archive}{2023 -- present}
\org{Pilot contribution at Ohio State, 2023--May 2025; WHO contractor, Jun 2025--present; Key Personnel on the 2022--2026 archive award}
```

- Co-lead software development for the WHO-hosted Reference Data Archive with the Africa Health Research Institute as platform manager and core developer; serve as sole data manager (Julia, Python, R, SQL).
- Built data ingestion, curation, metadata, quality-control, and dissemination workflows, including NADA and user-facing APIs; manage platform users and data.
- Wrote the platform documentation (user guides, tutorials, standard operating procedures, protocols) and coordinate technical implementation across Ohio State, the Africa Health Research Institute, and WHO.
- Supervised two doctoral research assistants on data-quality checks, data cleaning, and coding.

```{=latex}
\role{Graduate Research Associate}{Jan 2019 -- May 2025}
\org{The Ohio State University; appointments supporting verbal autopsy methods, the Reference Data Archive, and customer-insights research}
```

- Dissertation: showed that fine-tuned pretrained language models using verbal autopsy narratives outperform leading questionnaire-only algorithms, and that multimodal models improve further; developed MultimodalVA, an open-source Python package for these workflows (\href{https://github.com/y-chu/MultimodalVA}{GitHub}).
- Led the cross-site analysis of harmonized verbal autopsy data from nine surveillance sites in six countries in eastern and southern Africa (first author, *Lancet Global Health*, 2024).
- Contributed statistical modeling to statewide COVID-19 prevalence estimation for Ohio using Bayesian multilevel poststratification with imperfect diagnostic tests (*PNAS*, 2021; *Annals of Epidemiology*, 2022).
- Contributed to NICHD-funded verbal autopsy methods research (R01HD086227), openVA algorithm validation, and the Bloomberg Data for Health Probbase update.

- Research Associate on the Maternal and Child Epidemiology Estimation and IMPROVE projects and on NICHD-funded studies of survey data quality (R21HD087811) and age patterns of under-five mortality (R01HD090082).
- Conducted systematic reviews, statistical modeling, and data analysis for global, national, and subnational estimates of child mortality and its causes (e.g., *Lancet*, 2016; *Lancet Global Health*, 2017), including a joint-first-author state-level analysis for India (*Lancet Global Health*, 2019).
- Coauthored a validation study of survey-reported neonatal mortality against surveillance records (*Demography*, 2020).
